style: Cut-paper and pastel scenes with text-relationship diagrams
provider: Built-in image generation and deterministic SVG diagrams
note: Pictures support the lesson text and do not replace decoding or evidence from narration. Key lesson word-part examples have native editable labels; other schematic marks illustrate organization. Read sort statements in their supplied context. Educator review is pending.

sources.prompt: Square text-free educational scene in layered cut-paper landscape style. A visibly narrow woodland footpath passes between dense ferns and bushes. Two simple pairs of small boot prints lie one behind another along the narrow path, not beside each other. Focus on the thin passage and vegetation. No people, letters, numbers, signs or photorealism. Muted greens, warm sand, ivory margin.
sources.alt: A narrow woodland path runs between ferns, with boot prints along its center.
sources.caption: In the sentence, single file suggests that narrow means not wide. The path illustrates that possible meaning; the footprints do not measure its width or the number of walkers.

sources.prompt: Square text-free educational still life in layered cut-paper and pastel style: a yellow lemon, green lime and orange orange arranged separately with one cut citrus half showing segmented flesh. All clearly recognizable, clean ivory background, ample separation. No labels, letters, numbers, people or photorealism. Illustrates examples of citrus, not exact proportions.
sources.alt: A lemon, lime and orange sit separately beside a cut orange half.
sources.caption: Citrus is a category that includes lemons, limes and oranges. The listed examples supply a clue; the picture is not a definition of every citrus fruit.

assets.prompt: Text-free literacy diagram: A middle line on a schematic page is gold, surrounded by four teal lines.
assets.alt: A middle line on a schematic page is gold, surrounded by four teal lines.
assets.caption: The highlighted position represents an unfamiliar word within surrounding text. Use the actual sentence for clues; these marks are not readable words.

assets.prompt: Text-free literacy diagram: A magnifying-glass outline highlights the middle of a schematic page.
assets.alt: A magnifying-glass outline highlights the middle of a schematic page.
assets.caption: Find the specific words that support a possible meaning, then reread to check it. A plausible guess still needs evidence.

assets.prompt: Text-free literacy diagram: One wide teal box points down to one wide gold box.
assets.alt: One wide teal box points down to one wide gold box.
assets.caption: A definition clue states a meaning. Add the target word and its definition as editable text, for example nocturnal and active at night.

assets.prompt: Text-free literacy diagram: One teal box branches to three gold circles.
assets.alt: One teal box branches to three gold circles.
assets.caption: Examples are cases in a category: citrus includes lemons, limes and oranges. Add the actual examples; three circles alone do not define a category.

assets.prompt: Text-free literacy diagram: Two matching teal blocks have a pair of short gold lines between them.
assets.alt: Two matching teal blocks have a pair of short gold lines between them.
assets.caption: Synonyms have similar meanings in context. Matching shapes are only a reminder; synonyms are not always interchangeable in every sentence.

assets.alt: A short teal column and tall coral column are compared with an arrow.
assets.caption: Short and tall contrast in this context. A contrast word can signal a clue, but does not guarantee an exact antonym.

assets.caption: For un-break-able, the prefix is un-. Add editable word parts. Not all words have three parts; do not strip random letters from the ends.

assets.alt: Three blank word-part blocks have the last position highlighted in gold.
assets.caption: For un-break-able, the suffix is -able. Add editable word parts. Not all words have three parts; do not strip random letters from the ends.

assets.alt: Three blank word-part blocks have the middle position highlighted in gold.
assets.caption: For un-break-able, the base/root is break. Add editable word parts. Not all words have three parts; do not strip random letters from the ends.

assets.caption: Weary and tired describe similar feelings after the hike. An object picture cannot establish a person’s feeling; use the words in the sentence.

assets.alt: A street between buildings contains no people or vehicles.
assets.caption: Deserted means empty of people here. The sentence contrasts it with busy; this does not mean every quiet street is completely deserted.

assets.caption: A sharing schematic supports the generous/stingy contrast. Amount alone does not show generosity; circumstances and the sentence matter.
